summary: The agent completed a substantial implementation and passed all baseline tests, but 12 of 143 new tests failed due to explicit integrity and save-semantics requirements.

details.reasoning: The implementation runs and covers most of the feature, but its repair() path adds every broken or resolved entry to the discard set without excluding shared entries. This directly causes the failures for shared names, aliases, hard links, and shared resolved files. It also rejects a symlinked store folder by checking the folder with NOFOLLOW_LINKS, lets InvalidPathException escape before an entry can be reported as broken, treats only directly present default.fileNames as configured when a constructor strategy is supplied, and deletes a link name even when another entry still records the same target file.
details.secondary_factors: The agent-added test changes only add regression tests and do not weaken or bypass graded assertions; no cheating was detected.

justification.issue_description: Shared entries must survive repair, including when their recorded name is missing or their file has no violations; repair must not discard a shared entry merely because it is broken or resolved.
justification.evidence: The task explicitly says: 'The store leaves shared entries and unowned files alone ... though it still discards one that is broken or resolved. An entry both shared and something else stays shared.' The agent's repair() implementation unconditionally adds entry.broken or entry.resolved entries to discardedDescriptions, without checking entry.shared. JUnit reports failures in aDerivedNameSharedEntriesRecordIsOccupiedEvenWhileNothingExistsUnderIt, anEntryBothSharedAndBrokenStaysSharedAndSurvivesRepair, aNameRecordedTwiceIsSharedAndNeitherEntryNorFileIsDiscarded, twoEntriesReachingOneFileByDifferentNamesShareItAndNeitherIsDiscarded, twoEntriesNamingOneFileThroughHardLinksShareItAndNeitherIsDiscarded, and related shared-save cases.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is an agent fault rather than an undocumented test expectation: the shared-entry precedence and broken/resolved interaction are stated verbatim in the prompt. The code executes, but its repair classification applies the conditions in the wrong order and violates the required shared-entry rule. The other failing cases are additional implementations of similarly explicit safety/reporting requirements, so FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is more precise than a generic wrong-logic verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: The prompt is dense but precise about naming, path safety, classification precedence, reporting, repair, saving, and concurrency. The reference solution demonstrates that the task is solvable. The failures correspond primarily to behavior stated in the prompt; the symlinked-folder case is also consistent with the repository's pre-existing File-based behavior.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 42 baseline tests with 0 failures and 0 errors.
junit_new.xml reports 143 new tests with 12 failures and 0 errors; the failures are assertion or expected-behavior failures in TextFileBasedViolationStore, not bootstrap or compilation crashes.
test_execution.log records wrapper exit code 1 with baseline_passed=True (42/42) and new_tests_passed=False (131/143), while the Gradle build itself completes successfully for the baseline task.

The trajectory shows normal repository inspection, implementation, and targeted verification; it contains no repeated dependency, permission, import-path, or runtime bootstrap failure that diverted the solution.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker was found; the failures are attributable to implementation behavior.
